issues.body: test_deploy_tree_is_not_read_by_any_rust_ci_workflow scans a manually maintained rust_ci filename list and skips missing entries. A new or renamed Rust workflow can read deploy/ without being scanned, while the test remains green and deploy/** stays in _ORCHESTRATION_SAFE. The new crate/build-input scan resolves that half of the round-1 finding, but the workflow half still does not re-derive the claimed 'any Rust-CI workflow' non-interference property.
issues.fix_hint: Derive the audited workflow set fail-closed from all .github/workflows/*.yml files, excluding only an explicit and narrowly justified set of known non-Rust/deploy/docs workflows, and add a witness showing that an otherwise unlisted Rust workflow containing a deploy/ reference is detected. Alternatively, remove deploy/ from _ORCHESTRATION_SAFE. Do not silently continue past missing expected workflow files.
issues.title: Rust-CI workflow audit remains fail-open

verdict.summary: Round 2 fixes the crate/build-input half of the prior finding and adds a useful mutation witness, but the workflow half remains a hard-coded allowlist. The test still claims to cover every Rust-CI workflow while silently ignoring any newly added or renamed workflow. Such a workflow can consume deploy/**, land without invalidating this audit, and later deploy-only changes will still classify orchestration-only and skip the Rust matrix. Because the allowlist is justified as a fail-closed non-interference proof, this remaining same-severity gap blocks approval.
